content.text:
**Analyzing Line Colorations**

I'm currently evaluating the vertical lines. I've noted their positions and associated colors: line 1 at column 3 (color 4), line 2 at column 9 (color 3), and line 3 at column 17 (color 2). I'm also considering scattered points, like the one at r=0, c=5 with color 1, trying to determine if this color is also tied to line attributes.

**Connecting Points to Lines**

I'm re-examining how points relate to the vertical lines. It appears points adopt the color of the nearest vertical line and shift their position to be adjacent to that line. If no line of a point's color exists, that color is discarded.

**Refining Point Movement**

I've confirmed that points matching line colors move adjacent to their respective lines, while unmatched points vanish. This logic successfully predicted train 2's output. I'm now applying this to train 3, observing how existing points behave around the single horizontal line of color 8.

**Processing Test Input**

I've analyzed the test input, confirming that points matching line colors move horizontally to an adjacent cell of their line. Unmatched colors are discarded. This logic has now been applied to the test grid, and I'm observing the resulting point placements based on the vertical lines present.

**Refining Point Behavior**

I'm now meticulously re-evaluating each row and cell of the test input. I've confirmed that a point at (8,5) with color 2, near the color 2 line at column 17, will move right to column 16. Points without corresponding lines, like color 1 at (10,14), are discarded.

**Revising Point Adjacency**

I'm re-analyzing how points interact with lines. It appears points will move to the closest adjacent cell of their line's color, even if they have to "pass through" other lines to do so. This explains why the color 3 point at (11,16) landed near line 3 at column 3, not line 4 at column 12.
